title: Microburst-aware caching advisor with snapshot-based safe apply and rapid rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an automated advisor that recommends per-prefix cache key design, TTL profiles, and batching parameters that explicitly handle microburst traffic patterns. The advisor will produce safe config snapshots and support a snapshot-based apply flow (dry-run shadow, canary, automated verification gates) with an automated fast rollback path. Goal: reduce token cost by 10-25% on prefix-heavy workloads while keeping p95 generation latency within SLA and preserving end-to-end correctness.
background: Existing prefix TTL and keying playbooks assume steady-state traffic. We see recurring microbursts (traffic spikes lasting 5–60s) that cause either over-eager TTLs that evict when traffic rebounds or overly long TTLs that waste memory during quiet periods. Batching knobs are currently global and do not account for per-prefix burstiness. Past rollouts caused elevated tail latency when TTLs/keys were applied too eagerly (see incident INC-2025-09).
acceptance_criteria: Advisor outputs per-prefix recommendations (cache key template, TTL percentiles, batching window) for top 5k prefixes
Config snapshot can be applied to a shadow path with zero user-visible changes
Canary rollout to 1% traffic runs for 24h with automated gates and no manual intervention if metrics stable
Automated rollback triggers within 90s of gate breach (latency/500s/error rate thresholds) and restores prior snapshot
Simulation estimates show median cost reduction >=10% for at least two sampled workloads and no increase in p95 latency beyond SLA
technical_notes: We will model prefix hit behavior with a hierarchical Bayesian estimator that combines global priors, per-prefix observed counts, and burst detection features (burstiness score from EWMA of arrival rate). TTL suggestion will be a three-tier profile (short/medium/long) with annealing schedules. Batching advisor will suggest window and max_batch_size per model route, and include microburst-aware dynamic shrinking to avoid queueing during spikes. Config snapshots are immutable JSON blobs versioned in the config store and referenced by rollout jobs. Shadow apply uses a traffic-splitting layer to duplicate 1% of traffic to the candidate path. Rollback uses last-known-good snapshot and an expedited deployment path with prioritized traffic reassign. Metrics emitted: cache_hit_rate(prefix), ttl_eviction_rate(prefix), batching_queue_time(route), e2e_latency_p50/p95, tokens_per_request, cost_per_token. Use existing probing harness (ENG-617890) and extend it with microburst scenarios. Integrate with runtime-telemetry ingest and console dashboard for per-prefix diagnostics.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Unit tests + local sim (engineer) - verify advisor logic with synthetic traces
Stage 1: Shadow apply (0% serving) - duplicate 5% of traffic into candidate path for 48h, collect metrics
Stage 2: Small canary (1% live routing) for 24h with automated gates (p95 latency, error rate, cache_hit_rate)
Stage 3: Gradual increase 1% -> 10% -> 50% with 24h steady windows and automatic stop/rollback if gate triggers
Stage 4: Full apply at 100% with monitoring retention for 7 days and postmortem playbook readiness
rollback_plan: Rollback is snapshot-based. If a gate breaches, Orchestrator calls the fast-revert API which swaps route pointers to the last-known-good snapshot and restarts affected workers with expedited priority. For stateful cache changes that require TTL shrink/grow, we apply a compensating TTL anneal (30% step) to limit sudden cache churn. If fast-revert fails, escalate to on-call runtime team and follow manual rollback checklists in playbook RB-2026-04.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for Bayesian estimator and burst detector. 2) Simulation harness runs with historical traffic traces (week of spikes from project telemetry) and counterfactuals. 3) Shadow replay with production sampling for 48h. 4) Canary with synthetic microburst injection (stress tests) monitoring p95 latency, error ratio, cache evictions. 5) Chaos tests: kill candidate workers during canary to validate rollback speed. Links to test notebooks: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example-tests
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Architecture review with runtime and telemetry teams. Decided on snapshot immutability and shadow duplication at the ingress layer (notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COST/Microburst+Advisor+Arch)
2026-03-01: Prototype of burstiness score implemented; initial simulations show TTL annealing reduces eviction churn by ~18% on sampled workload
2026-03-05: Integration PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/1829 (advisor core + snapshot API). Requesting runtime owners for review
2026-03-09: Telemetry schema updated to include cache_eviction_reason and batching_queue_time (schema PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/411)
2026-03-10: Began shadow apply on internal staging with 2% duplicated traffic; observed no regression for control routes, collecting per-prefix reports
notes_for_reviewers: Please focus reviews on snapshot immutability boundary and the safety gate thresholds. We intentionally tuned gates conservatively; we may relax thresholds after two successful canaries. Runtime owners: verify fast-revert path latency under 3 minutes in your environment.
